title: Gamification

source.name: Wikipedia — Gamification
source.note: Đã rút gọn: chỉ giữ một số đoạn.

paras: Gamification is the process of integrating game design elements and principles (such as points, badges, and leaderboards) into non-game contexts in order to increase user engagement and motivation. It is a component of system design. Gamification has been used to improve organizational productivity, flow, learning, crowdsourcing, knowledge retention, employee recruitment and evaluation, usability, usefulness of systems, physical exercise, tailored interactions and icebreaker activities in dating apps, traffic violations, voter apathy, public attitudes about alternative energy, and more.

Gamification techniques leverage people's desires for socializing, learning, mastery, competition, achievement, status, self-expression, altruism, and closure, or simply their response to framing a situation as a game. Players are engaged using competition and rewards for completing tasks. Rewards can include points, badges, levels, progress bar, and virtual currency. Making the rewards for accomplishing tasks visible to other players (e.g., leaderboards) encourages players to compete. Meaningful choice, onboarding tutorials, increasing challenge, and adding narrative are other ways to make tasks feel more like games.

Points are basic elements of a multitude of games and gamified applications. They are typically rewarded for the successful accomplishment of specified activities within the gamified environment and they serve to numerically represent a player's progress. Various kinds of points can be differentiated between, e.g. experience points, redeemable points, or reputation points, as can the different purposes that points serve. One of the most important purposes of points is to provide feedback. Points allow the players' in-game behavior to be measured, and they serve as continuous and immediate feedback and as a reward.

Leaderboards rank players according to their relative success, measuring them against a certain success criterion. As such, leaderboards can help determine who performs best in a certain activity and are thus competitive indicators of progress that relate the player's own performance to the performance of others. However, the motivational potential of leaderboards is mixed. Werbach and Hunter regard them as effective motivators if there are only a few points left to the next level or position, but as demotivators, if players find themselves at the bottom end of the leaderboard. Competition caused by leaderboards can create social pressure to increase the player's level of engagement and can consequently have a constructive effect on participation and learning. However, these positive effects of competition are more likely if the respective competitors are approximately at the same performance level.

Performance graphs provide information about the players' performance compared to their preceding performance during a game. Thus, in contrast to leaderboards, performance graphs do not compare the player's performance to other players, but instead, evaluate the player's own performance over time. Unlike the social reference standard of leaderboards, performance graphs are based on an individual reference standard. By graphically displaying the player's performance over a fixed period, they focus on improvements. Motivation theory postulates that this fosters mastery orientation, which is particularly beneficial to learning.

Teammates, whether they are other real players or virtual non-player characters, can induce conflict, competition or cooperation. The latter can be fostered particularly by introducing teams, i.e. by creating defined groups of players that work together towards a shared objective. Meta-analytic evidence supports that the combination of competition and collaboration in games is likely to be effective for learning.

questions.q: What is the purpose of gamification?
options: To turn every kind of activity into an entertaining video game
To boost motivation by using game features in other kinds of activity
To replace teachers and managers with automated software
To record how much time users spend playing games
questions.explain: Đoạn 1: đưa yếu tố thiết kế game vào bối cảnh không phải game để tăng sự tham gia và động lực.

questions.q: According to paragraph 2, how do gamified systems encourage competition?
options: By hiding all scores until the activity has finished
By giving every participant exactly the same reward
By taking away every kind of challenge
By letting everyone see the rewards that others have earned
questions.explain: Đoạn 2: phần thưởng hiển thị cho người chơi khác (bảng xếp hạng) khuyến khích cạnh tranh.

questions.q: What does the writer identify as a key function of points?
options: Allowing players to exchange them for real products
Taking the place of badges and leaderboards
Giving players immediate information about how they are doing
Making tasks harder as players advance
questions.explain: Đoạn 3: “one of the most important purposes of points is to provide feedback”.

questions.q: Why is the motivational effect of leaderboards described as “mixed”?
options: They inspire players near the next rank yet discourage those at the bottom
They work only for players who have never tried similar games
They motivate beginners but bore the most experienced players
Players enjoy them, although game designers generally dislike them
questions.explain: Đoạn 4: Werbach & Hunter: có tác dụng khi chỉ còn ít điểm tới cấp kế tiếp, nhưng làm nản người ở cuối bảng.

questions.q: How do performance graphs differ from leaderboards?
options: They rank players by the number of points they have spent
They set a player against that same person’s own past results
They show which team has the largest number of members
They can be seen only by the people who designed the game
questions.explain: Đoạn 5: biểu đồ thành tích so sánh với thành tích trước đó của chính người chơi, không so với người khác.

questions.q: What do the findings in the last paragraph suggest?
options: Games that combine competition with cooperation tend to be good for learning
Teams are less effective for learning than individual players
Cooperation is useful only when computer-controlled characters take part
Competition should be avoided in every educational game
questions.explain: Đoạn 6: bằng chứng meta-analytic cho thấy kết hợp cạnh tranh và hợp tác có khả năng hiệu quả với việc học.

questions.q: According to the text, gamification has so far been used only in education.
questions.explain: Đoạn 1: được dùng trong nhiều lĩnh vực — năng suất tổ chức, tuyển dụng, tập thể dục, v.v.

questions.q: Gamified apps have been shown to raise the profits of companies.
questions.explain: Bài không nhắc đến lợi nhuận của công ty.

vocab.def: the state of being interested and involved
a list that ranks players by their scores
a symbol that shows an achievement
information about how well someone is doing
something that makes people want to act
something that you plan to achieve

coll.ex: in order to increase user engagement
work together towards a shared objective
at the bottom end of the leaderboard
